answer: A peer-to-peer agent market can require each identity to lock a scarce token in an escrow contract before it may submit bids. The contract records one active bond per key and slashable deposits for proven double-spending or coordinated fraud; a cheap new key therefore does not create a free vote or reputation. An inlet can route verified work across a bridge, while a prism of independent reviewers checks delivery before release. To overwhelm honest agents, an attacker must tie up real capital in every identity and risk losing it, making a Sybil swarm expensive rather than merely tedious.
